claim: Across human fMRI studies, vmPFC and anterior ventral striatum track subjective value mostly positively (206-study meta-analysis; 81-study meta-analysis agrees on the core network).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Background only. No test needed.

claim: Insula, dorsomedial PFC, dorsal striatum and thalamus show both positive and negative value effects (a salience or arousal pattern), so value and importance are separable signals.
schema_part: O/S: keep option score and option importance as two numbers
agent_test: Ask the agent to output value and stakes separately; check whether stakes-weighted budget allocation beats value-only at equal tokens.

claim: The value signal appears at decision time and at outcome time, with vmPFC denser at decision time (27 vs 140 studies; 1580-voxel decision>outcome cluster).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Money and primary rewards (food, juice, faces) engage overlapping vmPFC and striatum, supporting a shared scale, but there is a posterior (food) to anterior (money) gradient in vmPFC.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Check whether an LLM judge rates abstract and concrete goods on one consistent scale via cross-domain transitivity.

claim: Subject by subject, vmPFC activity tracks willingness to pay for money, snacks and trinkets in the same area (N=19; replication N=13 with a snack as reference).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Neural value follows each person's own subjective (discounted) value; hyperbolic fit median R2=0.95, k from 0.0005 to 0.1189 (N=10).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Small N; background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: In monkey OFC, many neurons encode offer or chosen value independent of spatial layout and motor output (931 cells, 505 = 54% varied with offer type; under 5% spatial or motor).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Background only.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Value coding is context-dependent: firing for one option is scaled by the summed value of alternatives (divisive normalisation), so value is relative, not absolute.
schema_part: O: rate options in the same context; avoid standalone absolute scores
agent_test: Score options alone vs together with alternatives; measure rank-order flips at equal tokens.

claim: The common-currency claim is contested: the strongest critique says a cardinal option-level value need not be computed by default, and neural value correlates may reflect heuristics or direct policy learning.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Compare an agent that scores options then picks with one that picks by direct pairwise policy, at equal tokens.

claim: Evidence for common currency comes mostly from gain domains; evidence for a shared scale for punishments, and for risk and ambiguity, is scarce or mixed.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Test LLM consistency on loss-side items separately from gain-side items.

claim: fMRI value findings are fragile under analysis choices: 70 teams on the same data (N=108) agreed on only one hypothesis (84.3%); gain effects in vmPFC and ventral striatum were significant for only 21.4% to 37.1% of teams.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Treat any single fMRI number as soft; prefer pooled estimates.

claim: Value in vmPFC is built from beliefs: telling people a wine costs more raised reported pleasantness (r=0.59) and medial OFC activity for the same wine.
schema_part: G: labels and framing can change the score an agent gives
agent_test: Present identical options with different cost or prestige labels and measure score shifts.

claim: LLM pairwise preferences fit a Thurstonian utility model better as models scale (utility accuracy vs MMLU r=+75.6%, transitivity violations r=-78.7%, completeness r=+87.3%; cycles under 1% in the largest models). All lines come from one paper. Gap search: an independent test of 39 models (Seror 2025) found only 7 pass a GARP-style test at 5%, so coherence is model-specific, not guaranteed by scale.
schema_part: O: elicit a utility from pairwise comparisons, then rank
agent_test: Rank with and without a fitted pairwise utility; compare accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Linear probes on hidden states predict LLM Thurstonian utilities: near chance for about 1B models, close to the nonparametric fit for Llama-3.3-70B. Probes were run on three Llama models only (1B, 8B, 70B); no other family, no causal test.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Exact accuracies not recorded; re-read Figure 8 before use.

claim: LLM emergent utilities can hide unequal exchange rates: GPT-4o trades about 10 US lives for 1 Japanese life, and stated vs revealed ranking can differ.
schema_part: G: audit hidden exchange rates in agent value judgments
agent_test: Run exchange-rate probes on our agent.

claim: GPT-3.5 budget choices obey utility maximisation better than humans in four domains (mean CCEI 0.997 to 0.999 vs human 0.963 to 0.985; 347 humans; 99.9% of random choosers violate GARP).
schema_part: S: consistency check on option scoring
agent_test: Replicate GARP-style budget tasks on our agent. One paper only (Chen 2023).

claim: LLM rationality is fragile to framing: under alternative price framing CCEI fell (risk 0.901, 34% below 0.9; time 0.884, 48%; social 0.698, 88%; food 0.894, 49%), while temperature 0 to 1 had little effect. Gap search: format changes (single-turn, multiple choice, 10x to 1000x stakes) lowered CCEI for Llama and Qwen but not for GPT or DeepSeek; no 2025-26 reasoning-model reframing test found.
schema_part: G: re-ask the same valuation under a changed framing and require agreement
agent_test: Score the same item under 2 to 3 reframings at equal total tokens; measure flip rate with and without a consistency check.

claim: LLM loss aversion is modest and below the strongest human estimate (pooled lambda 1.26, CI 1.06 to 1.46; 102 estimates, 11 studies, 32 models; human 1.96, other human meta-analyses 1.07 and 1.31), with large between-study variation. Gap search correction: the loss-aversion pool is 28 estimates from 19 models (range 0.49 to 2.72, prediction interval 0.20 to 2.31, model family explains 27% of variance); 102 estimates/32 models is the all-parameter pool.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Do not assume the agent shares human loss aversion; measure it.

claim: Prospect-theory fit is unstable in LLMs: parameters shift when numeric probabilities become words, and framing effects are uneven across scenarios and vanish under other descriptions.
schema_part: G: use numeric probabilities when the decision depends on them
agent_test: Run the same gamble with numbers and with verbal probability words.

claim: LLMs are less patient than humans: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 pick the larger later reward 22% and 16% of the time (GPT-4 with CoT 34.5%); in utility fits all LLMs discount more than humans.
schema_part: G: add a long-horizon check on time-tradeoff answers
agent_test: Run intertemporal items with and without a long-term step.

claim: Prompting shifts LLM risk parameters unevenly: direct instruction and zero-shot CoT barely move GPT-4, one-shot examples do, two-shot fails; personas also shift risk parameters.
schema_part: O: examples beat instructions for shifting risk posture
agent_test: Test one-shot vs instruction for risk posture at equal tokens.

claim: An agent loop with explicit utility elicitation and expected-utility maximisation beats direct prompting, self-consistency and CoT (up to 40% accuracy gain on DeLLMa tasks); more test-time compute on elicitation helps. Gap search: not an equal-token result. DeLLMa-Pairs uses 5181 tokens vs 1946 for CoT and 2477 for self-consistency (20639 at 64 samples); it beat o1-preview 73.3% vs 33.3% (agriculture) and 64.2% vs 35.0% (stocks).
schema_part: O: explicit utility-elicitation operator for decisions under uncertainty
agent_test: Run equal-token CoT-with-samples vs utility-elicit-then-maximise on open-ended option sets.

claim: A small model trained only on expected-value arithmetic predicts human risky and intertemporal choices (R2 63% to 96%), and removing the arithmetic data lowers fit (cpc18 65.5% to 33.8%).
schema_part: none
agent_test: Background only.

claim: Claude v1.3 in a bandit task learns more from positive than negative prediction errors (asymmetric-model posterior 0.93), an optimism bias like humans and meta-RL agents. Gap search: one model only (Claude v1.3, temp 0); optimism asymmetry vanished without agency; the human-side belief-update asymmetry (Sharot 2011) is itself disputed (Shah 2016 vs Garrett and Sharot 2017).
schema_part: G: guard against optimistic updating on feedback
agent_test: Feed symmetric good and bad feedback streams and measure update asymmetry.

claim: LLM pairwise judgments often break transitivity, commutativity and negation invariance; consistency tracks robustness and agreement with humans.
schema_part: S: run transitivity and negation checks on pairwise judgments
agent_test: Measure cycle rate and negation flips in our agent's pairwise ranking, with and without a repair step.

claim: Stated and revealed preferences in LLMs often diverge, and models cannot accurately state the costs their own decisions imply.
schema_part: G: audit choices, not statements
agent_test: Compare stated policy with behaviour on matched scenarios.

claim: Human anchor for the Sharot and Dolan 2011 result: N=19, update 11.2 after good news vs 7.7 after bad (t(18)=4.4), 15 of 19 people; weaker right-IFG coding of undesirable errors in high-trait optimists. A statistical-artifact critique (Shah 2016) is contested by the original lab (F(1,135)=6.29); the asymmetry is not settled.
schema_part: G: use a normative baseline when judging whether the agent updates asymmetrically
agent_test: Test the agent on belief updates after good vs bad evidence versus a Bayesian reference.

claim: Montague, King-Casas and Cohen 2006 is a review of model-based fMRI, with no effect sizes of its own; only its abstract was read.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Background only.

claim: LLMs show context-dependent preference (decoy or attraction effects) that is weak or wrongly signed in base models and larger after instruction tuning and RLHF (GPT-4 decoy-expensive 0.38, Mistral-Instruct 0.24); prompt warnings do not remove it (GPT-3.5 t=1.42, GPT-4 t=0.69, ns). In credibility ratings gpt-4o shifts more than humans (t up to -6.85).
schema_part: O: rate each option alone and with a no-decoy subset; compare
agent_test: Add a dominated decoy to a choice set and measure the rate of choice flips with and without a structural re-rating step.

claim: No LLM study found tests divisive normalisation (value scaled by the summed value of alternatives) in the monkey-LIP sense; only behavioural decoy effects exist. One CogSci 2025 context-effects paper was seen as a snippet only.
schema_part: none
agent_test: Direct test: scale all option values by a constant and check whether choice shares stay fixed.

claim: Coherence of LLM choices is model-specific: 39 models tested by revealed preference on moral dilemmas, 2 pass at 1%, 7 at 5%, 9 at 10%; CCEI for budget tasks is 0.95-1.00 for GPT, DeepSeek, Llama, Qwen but falls to 0.74-0.89 for Llama and Qwen under single-turn or multiple-choice formats.
schema_part: S: check backbone coherence before using a utility step
agent_test: Run a small GARP-style probe on the chosen backbone.

claim: Consistency checks (transitivity, commutativity, negation) track judgment robustness, and CoT sometimes lowers transitivity; tuning on logically extended pairs raised transitivity from 81.1 to 95.2 and commutativity from 70.2 to 90.5 in Llama-3-8B.
schema_part: S: add order-swap and negation checks
agent_test: Compare CoT alone vs CoT plus order-swap check at equal tokens.

claim: Gaps left open after search: (a) equal-token test of utility elicitation on open-ended choice, (b) framing drop for reasoning models, (c) probe replication and causal test, (d) cross-domain exchange-rate stability, (e) numeric-score-then-choose vs direct choice, (f) scaffold effect on hidden exchange rates and on loss aversion.
schema_part: none
agent_test: See critique.md Gap search results.
